More famous mythological ones include Ilmarinen in the Kalevala, who creates for himself a woman of gold after the death of his wife and crafts the Sampo, and Volund in the Norse sagas, who creates Sigurd's sword Gram. Originally practiced in Greek myth by Brontes, Arges, and Steropes, identify this profession, whose most famous mythological practitioner is probably Hephaestus.

Antigonus II Gonatas repelled an invasion by this man, who was then called to Greece by the pretender Cleonymus to oust King Areus from Sparta. He first became involved in conflict on the Italian peninsula when Tarentum attacked Thurii, burned a Roman fleet in its harbor, and called in this man. Appius Claudius refused the peace terms of this man's ambassador Cineas despite the fact that the Lucanians, Samnites, and Bruttians joined this man after his victory over Rome at Heraclea, and after his death at Argos in 272, his general Milo surrendered Tarentum. He is best remembered, however, for his victory at Ausculum, and his subsequent statement. Identify this king of Epirus, who after Ausculum remarked, "Another such victory and we are lost."

Sometimes bearing the epithet "Chestnut" because of the predominance of chestnut trees in the city in which it was centered, one of its primary instigators, Julia Tymoshenko, was confirmed as prime minister on February 4th. This event resulted in the ordering of a second round of run-off elections on December 26, 2004, following more than a month of demonstrations in front of the Verkhovna Rada building. Most protests took place in Kiev's Independence Square, and a second runoff election resulted in a loss for Victor Yanukovych. Taking its name from the color of the ribbons worn by supporters of Victor Yuschenko, identify this recent upheval in Ukraine.

Upon moving into Dorothy Day's Catholic Worker House of Hospitality, this man took over the Catholic Worker newspaper. Three years after his most famous work, he claimed that decadence resulting from unplanned social upheaval threatened to destroy Western civilization in The Accidental Century, and he outlined "a radical program for a new majority" in Toward a Democratic Left. He reprised that most famous work in The New American Poverty and The Next America, and it is that work, a 1962 analysis of poverty which provided the impetus for the Great Society, for which he is best remembered. Identify this American social commentator, best known for The Other America.

One battle of this name saw the destruction of the fleet of Licinius by forces under Crispus in 323 B.C., and in 1930, the name of this location was changed to Edirne. In 914, Tsar Symeon of Bulgaria captured it, only to lose it again, and it was sacked by Tsar Samuel in 1003 during the wars agains Basil II. In a more famous battle of this name, Fritigern emerged victorious, making the first break in the Rhine-Danube frontier, and an 1829 treaty of this name extended the Russian frontier on the Pruth and stipulated that Turkey withdraw all Muslims from Moldavia and Wallachia. Located in Thrace in modern-day Turkey, identify this city which lent its name to a 378 A.D. Battle that saw the death of the emperor Valens, and which is named after Hadrian.

It was first noted by Antonio Pigafetta and it was explored by Max Weber in the 1899 Siboga expedition, who revised its location from that given by its namesake. In the twentieth century, it was found to coincide with a plate boundary, which indicated that no land bridge could ever have existed between the two continental landmasses it separates. Introduced in the book Island Life, it separates Bali and Lombock, and species to the west of it are related to Asiatic species while those east of it are related to Australian ones. Identify this imaginary line that runs between Borneo and Celebes and is named in honor of a British naturalist who proposed natural selection independently of Darwin.

During his eight undistinguished years in the Senate, he was praised by Benjamin Tucker's revolutionary journal Liberty for introducing bills "pregnant with the economics of anarchism." His only electoral victory came when the "win the war" platform enabled him to defeat the pro-slavery John Downey for governor. His enormous vineyards were the location of Eadweard Muybridge's photography projects, which this man also financed. Alongside Mark Hopkins, Collis Huntington and Charles Crocker, he formed a group known as the "Big Four," serving thirty years as president of their venture, the Central Pacific Railroad. Name this hammerer of the Golden Spike, who founded a university in Palo Alto, California.

His general Rumiñavi's potential to lead a revolt led to his death at "El Cuarto del Rescate," a room that is preserved at Cajamarca. Francisco Pizarro got his room full of gold but still executed what Incan emperor?

The day on which this man vanished from his city is called the Flight of the People and the Nones of the Goats. He single-handedly killed over 7,000 Veienites at the battle of Fidenae, and after killing Hostilius he married his widow, Hersilia. A man named Julius Proculus claimed to meet him on the road after his death and told his people that he wished to be worshipped as the god Quirinus, which is sometimes associated with his father, Mars. He was originally abandoned because he was thought to be a threat to his great uncle Amulius, but he was suckled by a she-wolf along with his twin brother. For 10 points name this mythical founder of an eponymous city on the Tiber and brother of Remus.

Among his successes were dispatching Domitius Corbulo to subjugate Tiridates, the king of Armenia. He was not able to finish his planned Golden House covering a third of Rome, and his problems may have been rooted in the fact that Sextus Afranius Burrus proclaimed him emperor without any attempt to win popular support. Although the rebellion of Julius Vindex drove him to stab himself in the neck, Galba was the one who first took the throne upon this man's death. Identify this object of the Pisan Conspiracy and last of the Julio-Claudian emperors, a persecutor of Christians who may have moonlighted as an innapropriate fiddler.

The British Royal Engineers built the Vagar Airport here during World War II, getting further than the abandoned attempt at a Gothic cathedral at Kirkjubøur. A nationalistic period here in the 1850s led to the creation of a written language by Venceslaus Hammershaimb and the restoration of the Lagting. Suduroy is the farthest south, Lítla Dímun is the only one of eighteen uninhabited, and Streymoy is home to its capital, Tórshavn. Situated in the heart of the Gulf Stream in the North Atlantic, they lie northwest of Scotland and halfway between Iceland and Norway. Name this group of volcanic islands, a dependency of Denmark.

One side began by entering the Gulf of Ambracia and using the nearby towers and a line of ships to guard its entrance. This fleet consisted mainly of tall quinqueremes with bronze plating to protect them from ramming, while the opposing fleet was made up of more maneuverable Liburnian ships. Unable to damage each other, the navies resorted to firing spears and arrows at each other until the commander's lover fled with 60 ships toward Egypt, after which Agrippa gave chase and burned the remainder of the fleet. Name this 31 BCE battle, a decisive victory by Octavian over Marc Antony.

She killed her first six children in a cauldron, attempting to burn away their mortality. Along with Euronyme, this goddess caught Hephaestus when thrown out of heaven, and she also aided the Argonauts in passing through the clashing Rocks. Loved by both Zeus and Poseidon at one time, she was unable to marry an Olympian due to the prophecy of that she would bear a son greater than his father One of Nereus's fifty daughters, this sea nymph warned her son by Peleus against going to war. Name this woman who immortalized her son Achilles by dipping him into the river Styx.

This term may have come back into use when Richard Feynman used it as an analogy for pseudoscience. After he told Catherine the Great news of a Russian victory, the monarch sent this man to England, where he was a guest of Adeline Amundeville. His writings include Parliament and Revolution and Socialism: Critical and Constructive. His political fortunes were damaged by the J.R. Campbell trial and the Zinoviev letter, a forgery that outlined a plot for a Communist revolution in England. Twice preceeded and twice succeeded by Stanley Baldwin, for 10 points identify this first Laborite Prime Minister of the UK, who shares his surname with the first premier of Canada.

His verse epic on the life and execution of Mary Queen of Scots gained him a doctorate in theology from the Collegium Sapientiae and the cross of the Order of Malta. He defended his decision to shun traditional dramatic norms in his The New Art of Writing Plays, and his first wife, Isabel de Urbino, figured into his poetry and plays as the character Belisa. Identify this author of The Sheep Well and about 1800 other plays of the Spanish Golden Age.

He served as United States Ambassador to Honduras from 1981-1985, during which time he influenced an increase in Honduran aid to the Nicaraguan Contras, and his mastery of Vietnamese so impressed Henry Kissinger that Kissinger chose this man to head secret negotiations during the Paris peace talks. The son of a Greek shipping magnate, he was an executive vice president for the financial services group McGraw-Hill before he returned to diplomacy. In his A Survey of the Summe of Christian Discipline, he espoused his preference for the Congregational model of church governance to the hierarchical Presbyterian structure. He preached for a time in the parish of Esther in Surry before becoming the lecturer to the Church of St. Mary at Chelmsford Essex. Known for a dispute with John Cotton and for drafting the Fundamental Orders, for 10 points identify this founder of Hartford, Connecticut.

This state's ruling house converted to Islam under the reign of King Kossoi, a member of the "dia" line which was supplanted by the "shi." It was strengthened in the late fifteenth century when the Mossi were repulsed and the Dogon and Fulani were defeated in the hills of Bandiagara, and it took Jenne in 1473 after a seven-year siege. It was weakened when Sultan Ahmad al- Mansur of Morocco raided its salt deposits of Taghaza, and its forces under Issihak I were routed by the Moroccans at the battle of Tondibi. Ruled from Gao by Sonni Ali and Muhammad I Askia, identify this African trading state in the Niger River region which arose after the decline of Mali.

In the guise of Isis, she served as the protectress of cemeteries and held a ladder by which the dead could climb to heaven. She was believed to descend from a sycamore tree to feed the dead upon their arrival to heaven, and she was sent by Re to wreak destruction on earth, but was so effective that Re had her drink beer so that mankind could be saved. With a name meaning "the house of Horus", for 10 points identify this Egyptian goddess of the sky and fertility, represented as a cow.

It resulted in a fourteen point declaration of rights that included a claim to a right of jury trial, and the right to petition the government. The ancient city of Palmyra serves as the setting for this man's second symphony, subtitled Antar. An Alborada, a gypsy song and an Asturian fandango compose his Capriccio Espagnole, while his Russian Easter Overture is dedicated to the memory of fellow might five composers Mussorgsky and Borodin. Name this Russian, the teacher of Stravinsky and composer of the Scheherazade suite and The Snow Maiden.

Before stealing from him Eddie Harris demonstrates a lack of reverence by saying "up your butt" to him. Later Eddie suggests that worshiping Jesus Christ would be more fruitful than following him. Name this Voodoo god worshiped by Pedro Cerrano in the film Major League.

Mr. Von Bubenberg led the Bernese forces into resolution of the Burgundian War at the Battle of Morat. Mr. Henri was a Merseybeat poet and conductor. The campaigns of Kaloyan shattered this movement, leading to its final retreat led by Geoffroi de Villehardouin. Inspired by the miracles of Fulk of Neuilly, it took shape at Ecry under the influence of Thibaud of Champagne and its first leader was Boniface of Montserrat, though it quickly lost fervor, leading to a lack of 24,000 ducats. Alternate arrangements were made with Alexius Angelus, who was strangled following one of its outcomes, the restoration of Isaac II, which occurred after the Hungarian port of Zadar was taken as a favor to Doge Enrico Dandolo. Its further actions would lead to the excommunication of its participants by Innocent III. What was this 1202 to 1204 crusade in which Constantinople was sacked?

In one legend, this being's life is saved due to a bid for immortality by Gajasura, and the date of his salvation is commemorated by the festival Chaturthi. His devouring of the city of Alakapuri results in the humbling of Kubera, and according to the Linga Purana, he may have been created to destroy the pride of the Asura tribe. As a scribe, Vyas Dev dictates the Mahabharata to him, and he wins his wives Buddhi and Siddhi by learning scriptures while tricking his brother Skanda into racing around the world. Name this son of Shiva and Parvati, the remover of obstacles of Hindu myth who has the head of an elephant.

This man nearly lost support for his passage of the Agricultural Land Reform Amendment Act, which redefined his country's sharecroppers as "small land owners." His sabotage campaigns introduced him to Colonel Preston Goodfellow, the primary force behind his rise to power, though his stint with the OSS is better remembered for the Hangang Bridge incident. In his first term, he seized the Dokdo Islands and outlawed the Progressive Party, while his third saw an attempt to prop up his appointed successor Yi Gi-bung through rigged elections exposed, leading to his resignation following the April Revolution. Throughout his rule he maintained his long-held belief that his country should remain united after the Treaty of Panmunjom. Name this first president of South Korea.

As there are twenty-two active volcanoes, along with many geysers and hot springs, it follows that the first geothermal energy station in Russia was built here. This province includes the southern part of the Kuryak mountains and contains the city of Petropavlovsk. Its eponymous peninsula divides the Sea of Okhotsk from the Bering Sea, and the Kurile archipelago stretches south from its tip toward Hokkaido. Name this province in far eastern Russian.

The stock for this company rose from 1/2 in January of 1720 to 1,000 in August of that year, and caused many greedy British investors, including King George I and Isaac Newton, to lose fortunes. Formed in 1711, this company was granted a monopoly on trade in South America by the British. Name this company whose collapse led Parliament to pass the Bubble Act, forbidding the issuance of stock in Britain.

To Socrates and his titular friend, the question of "what is justice" is pressing, as the Athenian ships are due back from Delos that very day. Socrates has not fulfilled the city's ultimatum to "either to persuade us or to do what we say," thus has he been sentenced to death for impiety. The friend fails to convince Socrates to let the guards be bribed so he can flee to Thessaly. For ten points name this dialogue by Plato, chronologically the last before the Phaedo.

In his Vatican trilogy, the Catholic Church survives two threatened nuclear wars, a prophetic Pope, a papal assassination, and even an early Second Coming. The first major novels of this Australian writer were Daughter of Silence and The Devil's Advocate, but he followed his greatest success with The Clowns of God and Lazarus. Name this author of The Shoes of the Fisherman.

There are four red and gold tapestries on the two sidewalls. The back wall has a doorway leading outside with a rectangular window on either side of it. The table in the center of the scene has a lovely blue tablecloth that seems to go unnoticed by the thirteen figures gathered around the table. Some of the men are deep in conversation and others are whispering, but most of them have focused their attention on the calm one sitting in the center of the table blessing the food. Located in the convent of Santa Maria della Grazie, FTP what is this Leonardo da Vinci work?

Its leaders, called "vicars in temporal matters," included Montefeltro of Urbino and Malatesta da Rimini. Peaking in the early Renaissance, over the next five centuries its power waned, and a 1929 treaty with Mussolini's government left only one of its members independent. Name this collection of Appenine and Latinian towns and city-states, whose last remaining state is the Vatican City.

As a joke, painter Giuseppe Arcimboldo once portrayed this deity as Austrian Emperor Rudolph II. Roman myth tells of his celebrated love affair with a nymph who allowed no suitors into her garden until, disguised as an old woman, he entered her orchards and fiercely wooed her. Receiving no response, he dropped his costume in despair, whereupon Pomona fell instantly in love with him and invited him to stay. FTP, name this minor immortal, the Roman god of fruits and vegetables.

Governors of this state include Fenimore Chatterton, Leslie Miller, and Alonzo Clark. A war over land rights and cattle theft against Nathan Champion and his followers, known as the Red Sash Gang, took place here in 1892 in Johnson County. One of three states to see the establishment of the world's first national park, it is probably best known for being the proving grounds of such political figures as Esther Morris and Nellie Tayloe Ross. Known as the "equality state," name this state, the first to recognize a woman's right to vote.

Emerging as larvae, members of this order undergo a metamorphosis via the pupal stage, during which time the forewings harden and thicken to form the elytra, which meet mid dorsum to protect the abdomen and hindwings. Mouthparts are modified for biting during this time, and in some species they may grow to assume antler-like proportions. Containing almost 330,000 species, it is by far the largest order in the animal kingdom. FTP, name this order of insects, comprising the weevils and beetles.

He won election to the House of Representatives in 1799 for his only term in that body. Prior to that point he had been on a diplomatic mission to France which precipitated the XYZ affair. In 1800, John Adams appointed him Secretary of State, a position in which he would seal the judicial appointment of William Marbury. To the west is the Gulf of Mannar, which receives the Aruvi Aru from this island. Important cities include its ancient capital at Kandy, the seaport Jaffna, and Dehiwala-Mount Lavinia. FTP name this island nation separated from India by the Palk Straight.

Born March 15, 1767, his colony of birth is disputed as the Waxhaw settlement lay on the border of North and South Carolina. After joining the revolutionary forces and receiving a scar from a British saber, he moved west and rose to prominence through the law. He was elected as the first representative to congress from Tennessee in 1796 at age twenty-nine. FTP name this future U.S. President who was known as the "Hero of New Orleans" and "Old Hickory".

Cathy bears Cal and Aron, abandons her husband Adam, and becomes a prostitute. It focuses on the life of the Trask family, which settles in the Salinas Valley in California. Based on the Biblical story of Cain and Abel, this is—FTP— what John Steinbeck novel?

From the period of 1964 to 1968, he was known as Abu 'Ammar, a cofounder of the Al-Fath movement. Earlier trained by Egyptian intelligence, he developed an idea of a fighting organization based on the Algerian model, and began to publish a newspaper, Filastinuna or "Our Palestine." For 10 points-- name this man who after revealing his real name, became chairman of the PLO.

According to research by Admiral Hyman Rickover, the ship's boiler plates were blown outward, likely a result of coal dust buildup near its powder magazine. These results, published in 1976, came 78 years too late, meaning the Hearst newspaper account of an enemy mine or torpedo held sway. For 10 points--name this ship whose sinking in Havana harbor helped precipitate the Spanish American War.

His memoir, Twenty Years of Congress, came following his resignation from the Cabinet after the death of President Garfield. Covered in those volumes were his ascendancy to the speakership in 1869, and his self-defense reading of the "Mulligan letters" which stained his reputation as leader of the "Half- Breed" Republicans, and blew his shot at the 1876 presidency. For 10 points-- name this multiply-nominated Mainer, who also served three presidents as Secretary of State.

This city is dominated by the mausoleum of Ahmad Shah Durrani, which sits next to the mosque of the Khirqah [keer-kah] that is said to contain the cloak of Muhammad. Located on the Tarnak River, it became the first capital of its unified country in 1747, and along with Peshawar is the center of Pashtun culture.
